methodological_rigor.justification: In vitro cell-based mechanistic study with appropriate methodology: two cell lines (AGS gastric cancer and HGEpiCs normal controls), parallel assays (ATP viability, ROS, GSH, MMP, AO/EB apoptosis, comet assay), IC50 determination by nonlinear regression, normality testing (Shapiro-Wilk), and appropriate statistical tests (one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc). At least four independent experiments per assay. However, no blinding reported, no in vivo validation, and TQ-ox derived from prior unpublished synthesis work (reference 8 appears to be author's own work), limiting independence of mechanism validation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Cell-based preclinical pharmacology study mapping to LoE 5 (mechanistic in vitro work). TQ is established natural compound; oxime modification is synthetic derivative with prior use in melanoma, liver, ovarian, and lung cancer. Application to gastric cancer represents extension rather than novelty. Differential sensitivity between AGS and HGEpiCs (IC50 40.29 vs. 46.42 µM) is marginal—only 13% difference, limiting claimed selectivity. No patient correlation, animal model, or pathway targeting specificity demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods are detailed and reproducible: reagent catalog numbers, concentrations, incubation conditions, and assay protocols provided. Ethics approval obtained for in vitro work (2024/15-15/33-24/760). ARRIVE-adjacent compliance for cell-based work. However, data availability is minimal: no statement regarding raw data deposition; assays are commercial kits but no mention of open repositories; supplementary figures referenced (Figs. S1–S4) but not provided in normalized text. Replication would require access to synthesized TQ-ox from prior work (ref. 8).

novelty_literature.justification: TQ-ox is pre-existing synthetic derivative (from authors' prior work, ref. 8); manuscript documents dose-response cytotoxicity profile and oxidative stress mechanism in AGS cells. Identical experimental endpoints (ROS, GSH, MMP, apoptosis, DNA damage) already reported by same/related authors in melanoma (B16F10), liver (HepG2), ovarian (SKOV-3), and lung (A549) cancer models (refs. 8, 11, 17, 27). Gastric cancer (AGS) application is purely incremental; no new mechanism, no novel compound, no mechanistic insight absent from prior cancer-specific studies. Fundamentally duplicative across cancer types.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is clearly written with logical progression: Introduction motivates TQ and oxime chemistry, Methods detail all assays, Results section systematically presents dose-response data with quantitative p-values. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings against prior TQ-ox work in other cancers and acknowledges limitations (in vitro only, need for in vivo validation, additional GC subtypes). Figures and tables support conclusions; statistical notation consistent. Minor redundancy: Results section repeatedly describes dose-dependent effects without novel insight.

key_strengths: Comprehensive experimental battery covering multiple mechanistic endpoints (ROS, GSH, MMP, apoptosis, DNA damage) in parallel assays with appropriate statistical methods and at least 4 independent replicates
Use of normal gastric epithelial control cells (HGEpiCs) allows differential toxicity assessment between cancer and non-malignant cells
Detailed methods with specific reagent catalog numbers and concentrations facilitate potential replication
Transparent acknowledgment of limitations (in vitro only, need for animal models and additional GC subtypes)
key_concerns: Compound TQ-ox is not novel—previously synthesized by authors; manuscript documents identical endpoints (ROS, GSH, MMP, apoptosis, DNA damage comet assay) already tested in melanoma, hepatocellular, ovarian, and lung cancer models

Gastric cancer application is purely incremental tissue extension; no new mechanistic insight, no pathway discovery, mechanism (oxidative stress + mitochondrial dysfunction) identical to prior cancer types
Differential selectivity between cancer and normal cells is minimal: IC50 differs by only 13% (40.29 vs. 46.42 µM)—marginal selectivity insufficient for clinical development
No in vivo validation, no animal models, no pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics characterized
Data availability severely limited: no statement on raw data deposition; supplementary figures not provided; replication requires access to pre-synthesized TQ-ox from prior unpublished work
Study design purely confirmatory—identical experimental paradigm replicated across 5+ cancer types with no variation or novel mechanistic hypothesis
chief_reviewer.rationale: Technically competent but profoundly incremental in vitro pharmacology manuscript. TQ-ox and identical experimental endpoints documented in prior work (melanoma, liver, ovarian, lung); gastric cancer represents non-novel tissue extension. Marginal selectivity (13% IC50 differential) and lack of clinical translation pathway preclude publication in higher-tier venues. Rejection at Tier 4 appropriate.
